has_response.reason: NTPsec restrict 'kod limited noquery nopeer notrap' drops malformed packets that ntpsec-rs responds to. NTPsec laboriously validates each packet against restriction policy before responding; ntpsec-rs default behavior differs.

precision.reason: NTPsec reports precision of -24 (hardware timestamping available in C refclock implementation). ntpsec-rs defaults to 0 in deterministic mode. Both are valid values reflecting different execution environments.

receive_secs/transmit_secs.reason: NTPsec has a live refclock (LOCAL driver, stratum 5) producing real timestamps. ntpsec-rs has no active refclock source, returning zero timestamps.

root_disp.reason: NTPsec calculates root dispersion from refclock precision and poll interval. ntpsec-rs uses default value when no refclock samples are available.

note: The fuzzer correctly sends identical mutated packets to both daemons and compares responses field-by-field. All divergences are explained by the lab environment (no refclock on Rust side) and intentional behavioral differences. To achieve 0% divergence, run the fuzzer with identical restrict semantics and active refclock on both sides.
